source.title_or_context: HCM In patients with HCM, it is recommended that beta-blockers are continued in women who used them before pregnancy.313 I C Recommendations for the management of arrhythmias Acute management (intravenous administration of drugs) of SVT and AF Immediate electrical cardioversion is recommended for any tachycardia with haemodynamic instability and for pre-excited AF.12,306 I C Long-term management (oral administration of drugs) of SVT and AF Beta-1-selective blockers or verapamilb are recommended

table_assessment.assessment_notes: This page is a medication-bearing summary/duplicate spanning HCM, arrhythmia, hypertension, and venous thrombo-embolism sections. Medication rows were retained while non-medication cardioversion, hospitalization, and delivery rows were excluded.

entities.surface_form: women who used them before pregnancy

normative_assertions.notes: Continuation applies to women already using beta-blockers before pregnancy.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with HCM, it is recommended that beta-blockers are continued in women who used them before pregnancy.

header_path: Long-term management (oral administration of drugs) of SVT and AF

normative_assertions.notes: The row recommends either beta-1-selective blockers or verapamil for SVT prevention.

text_units.verbatim_text: Beta-1-selective blockers or verapamil b are recommended for the prevention of SVT in patients without pre-excitation on resting ECG.

header_path: Long-term management (oral administration of drugs) of SVT and AF

normative_assertions.notes: The retained fragment is the WPW-specific antiarrhythmic recommendation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Flecainide c or propafenone c are recommended for the prevention of SVT in patients with WPW syndrome.

header_path: Long-term management (oral administration of drugs) of SVT and AF

normative_assertions.notes: This row explicitly recommends beta-1-selective blockers for rate control.

text_units.verbatim_text: Beta-1-selective blockers are recommended for rate control of AT or AF.

header_path: Long-term management (oral administration of drugs) of ventricular tachyarrhythmias

normative_assertions.notes: This is the pregnancy/post-partum beta-blocking recommendation for inherited arrhythmia syndromes.

text_units.verbatim_text: Beta-blocking agents are recommended during pregnancy and post-partum in patients with long QT syndrome or catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of hypertension

normative_assertions.notes: The retained fragment preserves the aspirin dose and pregnancy timing window.

text_units.verbatim_text: Low-dose aspirin (100–150 mg daily) is recommended in women at high or moderate risk of pre-eclampsia from week 12 to week 36–37.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of hypertension

normative_assertions.notes: This fragment preserves the lower hypertension threshold recommendation.

text_units.verbatim_text: initiation of drug treatment is recommended at SBP >140 mmHg or DBP >90 mmHg.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of hypertension

normative_assertions.notes: This fragment preserves the higher generic-threshold recommendation.

text_units.verbatim_text: initiation of drug treatment is recommended at SBP ≥150 mmHg or DBP ≥95 mmHg.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of hypertension

normative_assertions.notes: The source expresses a preferred antihypertensive drug set via the source-style phrase "drugs of choice".

text_units.verbatim_text: Methyldopa, labetalol, and calcium antagonists are the drugs of choice for the treatment of hypertension in pregnancy.

entities.surface_form: drug treatment with intravenous labetalol, oral methyldopa, or nifedipine

header_path: Recommendations for the management of hypertension

normative_assertions.notes: The retained broad drug-treatment phrase preserves the severe-hypertension medication row.

text_units.verbatim_text: In severe hypertension, drug treatment with intravenous labetalol, oral methyldopa, or nifedipine is recommended.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of venous thrombo-embolism

normative_assertions.notes: The source explicitly covers both prevention and treatment of VTE.

text_units.verbatim_text: LMWH is recommended for the prevention and treatment of VTE in pregnant patients.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of venous thrombo-embolism

normative_assertions.notes: Enoxaparin is explicitly an example; no equivalence to all LMWH products is inferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: For high-risk women, it is recommended to give a weight-related prophylactic dose of LMWH (e.g. enoxaparin 0.5 mg/kg once daily).

header_path: Recommendations for the management of venous thrombo-embolism

normative_assertions.notes: Dose selection is tied to body weight.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended that the therapeutic dose of LMWH is based on body weight.

entities.surface_form: patients with severe hypotension or shock

header_path: Recommendations for the management of venous thrombo-embolism

normative_assertions.notes: The severe hypotension/shock restriction is explicit.

text_units.verbatim_text: Thrombolytics to manage patients with pulmonary embolism are only recommended in patients with severe hypotension or shock.

entities.surface_form: at least 36 h prior to delivery

header_path: Recommendations for the management of venous thrombo-embolism

normative_assertions.notes: UFH infusion is stopped at the stated time.
Normal aPTT is a pre-anaesthesia requirement.

text_units.verbatim_text: In high-risk women, it is recommended to convert LMWH to UFH at least 36 h prior to delivery and to stop the UFH infusion 4–6 h prior to anticipated delivery. aPTT should be normal before regional anaesthesia.
